name: Comoros
snapshot: An Indian Ocean island nation that has seen some 20 coups and attempts since 1975, now dominated by Azali Assoumani, who is grooming his son to follow him.
culture: Comorian culture blends Bantu, Arab, Persian and Malagasy influences, and Shikomori, a Swahili relative, is spoken alongside French and Arabic. The grand mariage on Grande Comore is a lavish, years-in-the-making ceremony that confers social status and can cost a family its savings. Women commonly wear the colourful shiromani cloth and protect their skin with a yellow paste called msindzano.
society: The islands produce much of the world's ylang-ylang, used in perfumes, plus vanilla and cloves. Many Comorians risk dangerous boat crossings to Mayotte, the fourth island of the archipelago, which stayed French and is claimed by the Comoros. Remittances from France are a big share of income.
situation: Azali Assoumani, who first took power in a 1999 coup, won a fourth term in January 2024 amid opposition boycotts and deadly protests. In 2025 he gave his son, Nour El Fath Azali, wide powers to coordinate government, widely read as preparation for succession; the move drew opposition outrage, and Azali has since denied planning to hand over power. The rotating presidency between the three islands, created to end separatist crises, was weakened by a 2018 referendum.
power: A federal presidential republic of three islands. The directly elected president heads the government; the governors of each island have their own administrations.
